claims.text: Retrieve-and-Discriminate Prompter (RD-P) synchronizes knowledge retrieval and discrimination in a unified model using knowledge graphs.
RD-P trains a prompter based on a pre-trained language model with shared parameters.
The retriever module in RD-P identifies relevant reasoning paths in the knowledge graph.
The discriminator module in RD-P evaluates reasoning path credibility through logical coverage calculation to instruct retrieval.
RD-P constructs prompts to guide LLMs in reasoning and answering questions using both retrieved and implicit knowledge.

evidence.description: we propose a novel method called Retrieve-and-Discriminate Prompter (RD-P), which leverages knowledge graphs (KGs) for trustworthy RAG by synchronizing knowledge retrieval and discrimination in a unified model.
we train a prompter based on a pre-trained language model with shared parameters.
The retriever identifies relevant reasoning paths in the KG
the discriminator evaluates their credibility through 'logical coverage calculation' and in turn instructs the retrieval process.
Prompts are then constructed to guide LLMs in reasoning and answering questions using both retrieved and implicit knowledge.

methodologies.name: Retrieve-and-Discriminate Prompter (RD-P)
methodologies.description: A RAG methodology that uses shared-parameter PLM prompters with integrated retriever and discriminator modules over Knowledge Graphs.

limitations.text: Large Language Models face challenges due to hallucination issues.
The misuse of irrelevant external knowledge in current RAG solutions can be misleading.
